Chapter 5: Trusting in a Bigger Purpose and Letting Go of Control
So, have you ever hit a wall—even when you’ve given it everything you’ve got?
There comes a point when sheer effort just isn’t enough. No matter how hard you work, plan, or push, some things just stay out of reach. And that’s tough—especially if you’re someone who’s used to making things happen through pure willpower and determination.
But here’s something to pay attention to: there’s another layer to success. It’s not just about effort—it’s about trust, surrender, and feeling connected to something bigger than yourself.
Picture this: someone who’s always been the planner, the fixer, the one who takes charge. For years, that approach worked—until suddenly, it didn’t. After a string of setbacks, they’re left exhausted and discouraged. No matter how hard they try to force things, nothing seems to move forward. Then, in a moment of quiet surrender, they finally let go—if only for a second. Instead of pushing, they allow themselves to just rest, to listen, and to trust that maybe, just maybe, things will unfold in their own time.
And here’s the thing: this shift doesn’t mean giving up or becoming passive. It’s about recognizing that you can’t control everything—and sometimes, the best opportunities show up from the most unexpected places.
When you let go of the urge to micromanage every detail, you start to notice new possibilities. You become more open to intuition, and you respond to life as it actually happens—not just how you planned it.
Now, a lot of us struggle with the idea of trusting the universe, fate, or even a higher power. It can feel risky—especially after you’ve been disappointed or hurt. But trust isn’t about blind faith. It’s about being open to the idea that help, inspiration, or opportunity might come from places you never expected.
There’s a story I love about someone who, after chasing financial security for years, decided to focus on what actually brought them joy. They started a small side project—not sure if it would go anywhere. And then, something amazing happened. Doors started to open. Connections and resources seemed to show up out of nowhere, and the project grew in ways they never could’ve predicted. Looking back, they realized the turning point wasn’t a new strategy—it was the decision to trust and let go.
Letting go of control also means releasing your grip on specific outcomes. Of course, it’s natural to want things to turn out a certain way. But when you’re rigid with your expectations, it can lead to disappointment and frustration. When you stay open to different possibilities, it’s easier to adapt, learn, and actually find satisfaction in the journey—not just the destination.
And here’s another side of letting go: forgiveness. Holding on to anger, resentment, or regret keeps your energy stuck in the past. But when you forgive—yourself or others—you free up that energy and put it toward growth. It doesn’t mean you forget or excuse what happened. It’s about choosing to move forward, without carrying those old burdens.
Trusting in a bigger purpose also means tuning in to your intuition—that quiet voice inside that nudges you toward certain choices, or warns you away from others. Most of us have had those moments when something just “felt right,” or “felt wrong,” even if we couldn’t explain it. By listening to those signals, it’s easier to make decisions that really line up with your deeper values and what you truly want.
So, as you move forward, remember: sometimes, the most powerful thing you can do is trust, let go of control, and stay open to what life wants to offer you.
